Container.Name: Maintainerr
Container.Overview:
Maintainerr is the janitor your media server doesn't have.
Libraries fill up. Users request a movie, watch it once, and never touch it again. Half-finished shows sit around for years. And somehow you're the one who has to decide what to delete.
Maintainerr does the deciding for you. Write rules for the stuff that's just taking up space - unwatched, unrequested, gathering dust - and it gathers those titles into a collection, gives everyone a grace period to catch up, then clears them from your media server, the *arrs and Seerr. Set it up once and forget it. Everything is automated!
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: plex jellyfin emby radarr sonarr seerr tautulli library cleanup media manager
Container.Requires: The container runs as user 1000:1000. Before the first start, run the following in the Unraid terminal (adjust if you changed the appdata path): chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/maintainerr

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: HTTP port for the web interface.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Persistent storage for the Maintainerr database and logs.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Timezone used for rule schedules and logs, e.g. Europe/Brussels.

Config.Name: Base Path
Config.Description: Set only when serving Maintainerr from a subdirectory behind a reverse proxy, e.g. /maintainerr.

Config.Name: UI Hostname
Config.Description: Address the web server listens on inside the container. Leave empty for 0.0.0.0; set :: for IPv6.

Config.Name: GitHub Token
Config.Description: Optional GitHub Personal Access Token for higher API rate limits when checking for updates (60/hr without, 5000/hr with).
